fixed.what: Half of this was already in the spec: decisions 5 and 29 say no wake source is ever killed. The missing half is now added: the alarm is re-armed by a token it reads. The token is run/acked.json (the sha256 of its bytes). Every status --endturn already rewrites that file, so no new file, writer or schema was needed. After each sleep, watch.mjs --alarm checks the token. If it changed, the alarm keeps the new token, adds 1 to rearms and sleeps again, with no write and no clock read. It exits 30 only after a whole period with no change. Files changed: CONTRACT.md (3.9, decision 5 amended, new decision 40), spec/watch.mjs.md, spec/status.mjs.md, tcb/watch.mjs.
fixed.test_added: tcb/test/watch.test.mjs 'M1 alarm: an endturn during the sleep re-arms the running alarm by its token; nothing is killed or replaced'. It runs a real endturn during an 8 s sleep and expects rearms 1. It fails with rearms 0 when the fix is disabled (checked by a mutation run). Also a control test (rearms 0 when no endturn runs) and status.test.mjs 'M1 endturn re-arms a live alarm by writing the token'.

fixed.what: status --reconcile now checks the alarm after it builds the status. When no live alarm of this ce exists (none, dead, another ce, or the process list is unavailable), it exits 1 alarm-missing and sets result.arm to 'alarm'. The status is still written and the rows are still reconciled. The coordinator then starts watch.mjs --alarm first. Files changed: CONTRACT.md, spec/status.mjs.md, tcb/status.mjs (armAtStart). Status tests T7, T8, T9 and T16 run on roots with no alarm, so they now expect exit 1 alarm-missing through a helper, recNoAlarm.
fixed.test_added: tcb/test/status.test.mjs 'M2 reconcile asks for the alarm at turn start: none -> exit 1 alarm-missing; a live one of this ce -> exit 0'. Checked by a mutation run: it fails when the check is disabled.

fixed.what: Half of this was already in the spec: a keyed event exits while its line is above acked_seq. The planner's own predicate is now added as a new non-urgent watcher class, 17 act-due, last in precedence. Its key names the act, and it is acknowledged like every other class, so an act the coordinator cannot take stays quiet and causes no busy loop. Row acts: replace-fence and replace-start (only when a slot is free and the run is not halted or draining), stop-request, stop-session, stop-verify (only once the sample is stop_verify_deltas ticks old), start-session, and bind. Run-level acts: handover (a drain line of this ce and no slot used), run-terminal, and events (an event line above acked_seq whose key is no longer active). Slots are counted with lib.slotCount and an empty process list, so no PowerShell runs each tick. Files changed: CONTRACT.md (1.4, 3.10, decisions 2 and 40), spec/watch.mjs.md, tcb/watch.mjs. Found along the way and fixed in status.mjs: nextOf looked for the stop sample under the row's epoch, but stop.mjs names it by the target attempt. The status T3 fixture was renamed to match stop.mjs. Two T10 watch tests now expect exit 17 (their stopped rows with a free slot are an act due) and assert no class 26.
fixed.test_added: Eight tests in tcb/test/watch.test.mjs named 'M3 act due: ...'. They cover replace-fence and staying quiet once acknowledged, full slots against a free third slot, stop-request and the limit and failed rows, the stop-verify sample age, start-session then bind, handover, and an orphan event. Checked by a mutation run: all eight fail when the fix is disabled.

fixed.what: This was already in the contract and spec, so no script changed. lib.slotCount (CONTRACT 4.10) counts an admitted, started or bound current attempt as one slot even when no process is found, and admit condition 6 compares live + unknown + unconfirmed against N_max. spec/admit.mjs.md gains test T6c and now names M4.
fixed.test_added: tcb/test/admit.test.mjs 'T6c (M4) the model trace: a zombie of a planned hand-over plus an admitted-not-started row fill N_max 2, so a third is refused'. It expects exit 6 slots-full with unconfirmed 1 and unknown 1. Without the reservation the count is 1 < 2 and the third row is admitted. Not checked by a mutation run, because the counting is in lib.mjs.

fixed.what: CONTRACT 1.2 now has a one-sided exception. A counted tick whose gap (now minus last_tick_at) is more than 2 delta is a paused tick and leaves hang_ticks unchanged. New calls still reset hang_ticks, and ticks_total and the other tick counts still advance. A missing, unparseable, negative or short gap counts the tick as usual. result.paused reports a paused tick. Files changed: CONTRACT.md, spec/watch.mjs.md, tcb/watch.mjs.
fixed.test_added: tcb/test/watch.test.mjs 'M5 pause discount: a tick more than 2 delta after the last one does not count toward hang'. Checked by a mutation run: without the fix the second tick exits 21. Also a control test: 'M5 pause discount is one-sided: a clock that went back counts the tick'.

fixed.what: replace.mjs fence now checks for a READY of the current epoch under the run lock for every reason except first and tainted, including handover, memory, cut and drop. The check applies when the row is at epoch E with a running attempt. A READY found gives exit 5 ready-wins, leaves the row unchanged and writes one refusal incident. predictFence makes --dry-run predict the same. lib.fence still checks failure reasons only. Files changed: CONTRACT.md (1.4 exit 5, 3.6, 4, decision 40), spec/replace.mjs.md, tcb/replace.mjs.
fixed.test_added: tcb/test/replace.test.mjs 'T5b (M6) a READY of the current epoch wins over every reason but first and tainted, a planned hand-over included'. It covers handover, memory, cut and drop each giving exit 5, a dry-run giving exit 5, and a control. Checked by a mutation run: five subtests fail when the fix is disabled.

tests.command: node tools/lane.mjs --label modelfix-U1-final-a --timeout-s 600 -- node --test --test-concurrency=1 tcb/test/admit.test.mjs tcb/test/stop.test.mjs tcb/test/replace.test.mjs ; node tools/lane.mjs --label modelfix-U1-final-b --timeout-s 600 -- node --test --test-concurrency=1 tcb/test/watch.test.mjs tcb/test/status.test.mjs tcb/test/handover.test.mjs
tests.output_tail: Run final-a (admit, stop, replace): 144 tests, 137 pass, 0 fail, 7 skipped as needs-app, about 146 s. Run final-b (watch, status, handover): 118 tests, 108 pass, 0 fail, 10 skipped as needs-app, about 232 s. Mutation runs (each fix switched off through a temporary env guard, since removed; no TCB_MUT is left in tcb/): 9 of the 11 watch M tests fail, and the 2 that pass are the controls. 5 of the 6 replace T5b subtests fail, and the one that passes is the control. The status M2 test fails. No temp root is left under tmp/. Logs: tmp/mf-final-a.out, tmp/mf-final-b.out, tmp/mf-watch-mut.out, tmp/mf-mut2.out. Return file: done/modelfix-U1.json. Notes: (1) I broke the lane rule once: a one-line string replacement in watch.test.mjs was made with node -e outside the lane. (2) Open point for the owner of stop.mjs: stop verify counts ticks without transcript growth, and a tick across a PC sleep is no evidence that a process stopped, which is the same reasoning as M5. (3) The coordinator instructions must say to run status --reconcile first, start the alarm when it reports alarm-missing, and act on status.json when the watcher exits 17. There is no coordinator brief under tcb/briefs to edit. (4) handover.mjs needed no change (only a spec note).

lib_change_requests: EXIT: add 'act-due': 17 (CONTRACT 1.4, decision 40, M3). Until then exitSlug(17) returns 'internal', so watch prints code 'internal' for exit 17. The exit code and reasons[].code 'act-due' are already correct. watch.test.mjs takes SLUG[17] from lib.EXIT, so its check becomes strict as soon as the slug is added.

fence(): widen the READY re-check from `failure && reason !== 'tainted'` to every reason except 'first' and 'tainted' on the running-attempt path (M6). replace.mjs already makes this check under the same lock before it calls fence, so this is defence in depth, not a blocker.
Optional: move a row's next act into one shared lib function. status.mjs nextOf and watch.mjs rowAct now hold two copies of the same rule, as runFlags once did, and decision 19 would put it in lib.
